response_text: To pass an argument into a thread, the user creates a struct or variable and passes its pointer when calling osCreateThread. The OS stores this pointer in R0 during stack setup so the thread receives it as a void* argument. Inside the thread function, the user casts and dereferences the pointer to access the actual data. This works because R0 is the standard register for passing the first function argument in ARM. By placing the pointer there, the thread starts with the right data automatically.\n
